hook.text: Drowsy driving causes about 100,000 crashes a year in the US alone.

buildup.text: A tired driver drifts across the lane line without correcting because their brain is asleep.

discovery.text: Lane-keeping systems use cameras to read road markings and steer the car back if it drifts.

twist.text: Early versions only beeped—modern ones actually turn the steering wheel to nudge you back.

climax.text: Cars with lane-keeping assist show clear reductions in sideswipe and head-on collisions.

punchline.text: The car steers you back while you're still waking up.

quiz.question: What does modern lane-keeping assist do when you drift?
options: Gently steers the car back into the lane
